title: Perfect Investigation
verdict: Every alibi broken, down to the toll receipt in his ashtray.
narrative: You put it to {accused} in order: the envelopes he held for seven minutes, the service call he booked, the toll booth, the code at the rear keypad. He asks for a moment, and then for his solicitor, and then tells you where the boxes are.
The bearer bonds are found in a lock-up in Millbrook, still in their Mercantile wrappers. Every piece of jewellery comes home but one.
Walter Kemp sends you a key on a ring, cut to open nothing. 'For the next locked door,' the tag says.

title: True Criminal
verdict: The right name, and enough to hold it.
narrative: {accused} is charged before the evening papers go to bed.
The case holds. His counsel makes the most of the alibis you never broke, and the jury takes two days.
Most of the bonds are recovered. Head office changes the dual-control procedure the following week.

title: Wrong Suspect
verdict: A careful case, built around the wrong person.
narrative: Your case against {accused} has a lie in it, a motive and a place on the timeline. It is still wrong.
The charges are dropped within the month. By then the bonds have been sold through three countries.
The file is reopened in the summer and handed to someone else.

title: Innocent Person Accused
verdict: An arrest to satisfy head office.
narrative: {accused} is arrested on Harbour Street in full view of the morning queue.
The charges are dropped. The name is already in the papers, next to the word 'vault'.
The Harbour Street thief is never caught. Mercantile quietly settles with the box holders.

title: Criminal Escapes
verdict: A million pounds walked out, and nobody followed it.
narrative: The evening papers run 'THE PERFECT CRIME?' across the front page. It turns out to be exactly that.
Whoever opened the vault knew its every procedure, and knew how thin a file you'd bring.
Case #049 is filed under Unsolved. The bonds surface in Zurich two years later.
